title: Head, People & Culture Business Partner, Ethiopia
description: THE OPPORTUNITY Reporting to the Director, People & Culture Business Partner, Programs, the Head, People & Culture Business Partner, Ethiopia will lead the full People and Culture (P&C) partnership agenda for the Ethiopia portfolio. The role will serve as a trusted adviser to Ethiopia leadership, translating Foundation and country priorities into integrated people, organization, workforce, talent, culture, and leadership actions. As the primary P&C point of contact for the Ethiopia portfolio, the role will provide hands-on support across the employee lifecycle and coordinate delivery with P&C Centre of Excellence, People Services, Legal, and other enabling functions. WAYS YOU CAN CONTRIBUTE Serve as the strategic P&C Business Partner to Ethiopia leadership, translating country and Foundation priorities into an integrated people strategy, roadmap, and delivery plan. Assess organization, leadership, and capability gaps and lead workforce planning for Ethiopia, including demand and supply analysis, headcount planning, critical-role identification, scenario planning, and the resourcing, skills, and leadership priorities required to deliver the country strategy. Work with Talent Acquisition to deliver recruitment and own sourcing and recruitment up to Lead level within agreed accountabilities. Lead organization design and redesign work for Ethiopia, including role clarity, job descriptions, accountabilities, decision rights, RACI, spans and layers, job-evaluation requests, and maintenance of the approved organization structure. Assess the people impact of transformation and organizational change, and lead local change, stakeholder engagement, communication, and adoption plans. Build a high-trust, inclusive, and accountable culture by translating engagement and employee-listening insights into prioritized actions with clear leadership ownership and follow-through. Lead performance and productivity processes in Ethiopia, including goal setting, performance-cycle communications, first-level calibration, recognition, performance improvement, onboarding goals, and probation confirmation within scope. Build people-leader capability through coaching, facilitation, practical tools, and targeted learning, including support for difficult conversations with employees. Lead Ethiopia talent reviews and succession planning, ensuring critical roles have credible succession coverage and employees have clear development and career actions. Manage the annual pay-review process for Ethiopia and prepare recommendations for promotions, lateral moves, new roles, and acting or additional-responsibility arrangements within delegated authority, escalating exceptions to Total Rewards. Use workforce data, dashboards, and qualitative insight to identify trends, test assumptions, and provide evidence-based recommendations to Ethiopia leadership; maintain strong data quality and timely reporting. Manage employee-relations matters, including performance counselling, grievances, disciplinary processes, workplace concerns, and exits, in line with Ethiopian employment legislation, the Ethiopia Employee Handbook, and Foundation policies, ensuring fairness, confidentiality, due process, and appropriate documentation, and coordinating specialist Legal or Employee Relations advice where required. Identify, assess, escalate, and manage people risks across Ethiopia, including workforce continuity, employee relations, compliance, capability, leadership, culture, and change risks. Partner with P&C Centres of Excellence, People Services, Legal, Finance, and other enabling functions to provide an integrated and consistent employee experience while adapting appropriately to the Ethiopia context. Contribute Ethiopia insights to the broader P&C Business Partnering and Programs P&C agenda, and share practical learning across portfolios. WHO YOU ARE Postgraduate degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, Organizational Development, or a related field, and/or an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience. A professional Human Resources qualification or membership in a relevant professional body is an advantage. 10–15 years of progressive P&C or Human Resources experience in strategically focused roles, including essential senior-level HR Business Partner experience and a minimum of 5–7 years leading and developing teams with evidence of building capability, accountability, and engagement. Demonstrated experience supporting a complex country program or business portfolio in Ethiopia or a comparable African context, with working knowledge of Ethiopian employment practices and experience managing sensitive employee-relations matters with appropriate specialist support. Experience leading workforce planning, organization design and change, talent and succession, performance, and culture interventions, with a practical understanding of role clarity, decision rights, governance, and adoption. Depth in one or more additional P&C disciplines, such as Talent Acquisition, Reward, Leadership Development, or HR Services. Strategic business partnering and consulting skills, with the ability to connect business strategy to people, organization, and workforce choices, supported by problem-solving, facilitation, coaching, negotiation, and stakeholder-influence skills, including constructive challenge with senior leaders. Strong analytical and conceptual thinking, with experience using people data and qualitative insight to interpret workforce trends and organizational risks and to inform decisions. Able to navigate ambiguity and a complex matrix, working effectively with P&C Centres of Excellence and People Services teams while balancing enterprise standards with the Ethiopia operating context. High professional judgement, discretion, integrity, and cultural sensitivity when handling confidential or sensitive matters. Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills in English. Proficiency in Amharic or another Ethiopian language is an advantage. Demonstrates commitment to Mastercard Foundation’s values and to building an inclusive, respectful, and high-performing workplace. The Mastercard Foundation values the unique skills and experiences each individual brings to the organization and we are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive and accessible environment for everyone. Completion of satisfactory business references and background checks are essential conditions of employment.
